name: OrderChop
tagline: A hosted order intake and fulfillment tracker for small commerce and food-service operations, as far as its name and pitch go.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Order management is one of the most-built CRUD shapes in existence: items, orders, statuses, a board, a printable ticket. An agent will hand you a working local version of that in one sitting, and for a single operator running orders out of a spreadsheet today, that is already an upgrade. The part that does not come free is everything touching the outside world: Shopify or Stripe or WooCommerce webhooks, delivery platform feeds, printer hardware, SMS notifications, and staff accounts on phones. Those are each a small project, and together they are the reason hosted order tools exist. Treat the DIY build as your own back office, not as a replacement for anything that has to talk to a storefront or a courier.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you create orders with line items, move them through a status board, and print or export a prep ticket.
requirements: A machine that stays on if more than one person needs to see the board
API keys for any storefront or payment integration you actually want, in .env
whatYouLose: Webhook-ready integrations with storefronts, payment processors, and delivery platforms
Multi-user access with roles, so staff can update orders without touching your database
A mobile-friendly, always-on hosted board that survives your laptop closing
Customer-facing notifications: order confirmations, status texts, receipts
Someone else's problem when the printer, the webhook, or the timezone math breaks
moatNotes: Order tools get sticky fast because live operational data plus trained staff is painful to move, not because the software is clever.
whyPeopleStillPay: Order software is bought during a shift, not during a planning meeting. When tickets are stacking up, nobody wants to debug their own webhook handler or explain to a new hire why the board only loads on the owner's laptop. Paying gets you an uptime promise, a phone-shaped interface, and plumbing into the channels orders actually arrive through, which is the whole job. The build is easy; the being-reliable-at-7pm-on-a-Friday part is what the invoice covers.
notes: The CRUD is a weekend; the integrations and the uptime are the product.
prompt:
Build a local-first order management app for a single small business operator.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript
- Tailwind CSS for styling, no component library
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/orders.db
- Drizzle ORM for schema and migrations
- Zod for input validation
- Runs with: npm install, npm run dev, on localhost only

Data model:
- customers: id, name, phone, email, notes
- products: id, name, unit_price_cents, active
- orders: id, customer_id, channel (walk-in | phone | web), status (new | confirmed | prepping | ready | delivered | cancelled), due_at, notes, created_at
- order_items: id, order_id, product_id, qty, unit_price_cents, item_notes

Features in scope:
- A kanban board of orders grouped by status, drag or button to advance status, each card shows customer, item count, due time, and a red flag when due_at is past
- Order create and edit form with line items, live subtotal, and a free-text kitchen note per line
- Customer and product CRUD, products can be deactivated but not deleted
- A printable order ticket route (/orders/[id]/ticket) styled for 80mm thermal width with a plain browser print dialog
- CSV import for products and CSV export for orders in a date range
- A day view: today's orders sorted by due_at, plus counts per status
- Seed script with 6 products, 4 customers, and 10 orders across statuses

Explicitly out of scope, do not build or stub:
- User accounts, auth, roles, sessions
- Payment processing, Stripe, or any storefront integration
- SMS or email notifications
- Telemetry, analytics, cloud sync, deployment config

Rules:
- No secrets needed, but create .env.example with DATABASE_URL and read it if present
- Store money as integer cents everywhere, format only at render time
- Handle timezones with a single TZ constant in one config file
- Write a README with setup, the seed command, and a short list of what is deliberately missing
